fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Eleven Books in Eleven Years, and a Book With No Prerequisites", "body": "Dylan Saccoccio joins Chance Garton on the night his eleventh book in eleven years, The Real Universal Empire, goes live, work he built in small increments while holding two jobs in one of the most expensive cities in the world. He frames this one as deliberately accessible, something a sixth grader or a teacher could hand out for summer reading, with no need to have read the Spirit World series first. The first chapter drops free on his Substack the next morning as a three in one release: narrated audio, searchable digital text, and visuals of the locations and artifacts discussed."}, {"title": "Invisible by Proximity, and the Denial Underneath It", "body": "Chance describes his tuning practice, including a recent run of clients reporting improved eyesight, and a session where he traced a woman's recurring pattern back to a childhood crush who mocked her nose, followed by two later injuries to the same spot. Dylan calls it a perfect illustration of how things become invisible by their proximity, the way you can always see your nose yet almost never notice it, and argues that denial sits at the root of most mental and physical trouble. He also relays Sammy Gravano's line that a spoken word, like a fired bullet, cannot be called back mid course."}, {"title": "The Etruscan Argument Against a Greek or Oriental Origin", "body": "In the chapter one excerpt played on air, Saccoccio argues that the Etruscan languages are indigenous to Italy, that their alphabets are Pelasgian or Phoenician, and that no archaeological evidence supports mass migration into Italy at the turn of the first millennium BC. He contends Urnfield culture spreads south to north inside Italy, that Caesar is an exclusively Etruscan name, and that the term Phoenician derives from the Etruscan word for purple. He cites Suetonius, who wrote that aesar meant God in Etruscan, and says his own line runs back through Domenico de Cesare, born in Sicily in 1871."}, {"title": "A Bronze Hand, a Rattlesnake Disc, and Contact Before Columbus", "body": "The two examine a newly published 2,100 year old sheet bronze severed hand from the Basque region of Spain. Saccoccio's first read is that the characters look like Etruscan letters upside down, with proto runic forms of the kind that came out of Clusium, and he argues the Basques descend from Etruscans, pointing to aita, the Basque word for father. He then walks Chance to a Carthaginian stele on the Louvre site showing a palm with an eye, sets it beside the Tuscaloosa rattlesnake disc dated to 1300 AD, and calls the pairing either archaeological fraud or contact two centuries before Columbus."}, {"title": "Coined Words, Forged Centuries, and Leaving the Conspiracy Crowd", "body": "Reading from Archbishop Richard Trench's On the Study of Words, Saccoccio notes that Eichhorn coined the label Semitic barely three centuries ago simply because a common name was wanting. He argues the Latin Vulgate contains words already archaic by the Common Era, questions dating methods after rock formed thirty years ago was aged at millions, and locates the real disruption somewhere in the Middle Ages rather than with the Romans themselves. He closes saying he is done courting conspiracy theorists, wants serious readers and even critical guest writers, and measures his work by whether readers stop needing him."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The great Dylan Saccoccio launched his newest book today, The Real Universal Empire, and he's back on Vibe Rant to talk about the research within it! Cutting through the farrago of history and myth, T.R.U.E. explores artifacts, architecture, and language, to bring our understanding closer to reality when it comes to the origins and bones of our global civilization. By rectifying European history and better understanding our ancestors, what can we learn about ourselves?
